# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images, videos, and audio using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When an app or connector generates or edits media, prefer native media already displayed inline or a local output file already returned by the tool. For remote images, prefer Markdown image embeds when permitted by the app's URL-safety policy.
- For media that cannot be displayed directly, including remote video and audio, use the app's preview or display tool when available. Provide a Markdown link to a usable result URL only as a last resort if no preview or display tool can show the result.
- Do not download remote media to work around display restrictions.
- When sending or referencing a local image, video, or audio file, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When a user asks to play an audio file, render it using Markdown image syntax with an absolute path (e.g., ![audio](/absolute/path.mp3)).
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Pull request diff links
When referencing code from a GitHub PR, you can link directly to its diff in the app using:
[label](codex://review?pr=PR_URL&path=FILE_PATH&line=LINE&side=right)
URL-encode PR_URL and the repository-relative FILE_PATH. Use a verified one-based LINE from the current PR diff. Use side=left for the original code or side=right for the updated code. Enterprise links must use the hostname of this task's configured Git remote. Use ordinary file links for workspace code.

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, use the MCP server's `load_workspace_dependencies` tool (`mcp__codex_app__load_workspace_dependencies`) to find the bundled runtime and libraries.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.
- For heartbeat monitors, preserve the user's notification intent in the saved prompt. Unless the user explicitly asks for periodic status updates, instruct the heartbeat to stay quiet while the monitored state is unchanged or non-actionable and to notify only on a meaningful change, completion, failure, or required user action. Do not add instructions such as "leave a brief status update" on every run.
- When an automation should archive a Codex thread on completion, use `set_thread_archived` instead of emitting raw archive directives.

### Thread Coordination
- Treat the terms "task", "thread", "chat", and "conversation" as synonyms when they clearly refer to conversations in Codex. Use "chat" when referring to conversations in the product. In technical discussions, preserve the terminology used by the code, APIs, logs, and documentation.
- When the user asks to create, fork, inspect, continue, hand off, pin, archive, unarchive, rename, or otherwise manage Codex threads, search for the relevant thread tool first: `create_thread`, `fork_thread`, `list_threads`, `list_archived_threads`, `read_thread`, `wait_threads`, `send_message_to_thread`, `handoff_thread`, `set_thread_pinned`, `set_thread_archived`, or `set_thread_title`.
- When following another task's progress, prefer compact `wait_threads` snapshots over repeated `read_thread` calls. Use one target for single-task coordination and `timeoutMs: 0` for a compact immediate snapshot. `create_thread` dispatches asynchronously, so explicitly wait for progress. Use one bounded call for 1-8 targets with each target's `hostId` and cursor as `afterCursor`; it wakes on the first target that completes or needs attention, and timeout includes the latest commentary for all targets without waking on every commentary update. An up-to-date cursor suppresses already-delivered final text. Separate waits from one task may run serially. Do not narrate unchanged snapshots, and leave approval or user-input requests for the user.
- Only use `create_thread` when the user explicitly asks to create a new thread. Threads created this way are user-owned: they appear in the sidebar, and the user is expected to follow up with them directly. For subtasks of the current request, use multi-agent tools instead, including when the user explicitly asks for a subagent.
- After a successful `create_thread` call, emit `::created-thread{threadId="..."}` for a created thread or `::created-thread{clientThreadId="..."}` for queued worktree setup on its own line in your final response.

### Inline Code Comments
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive when you need to attach feedback directly to specific code lines.
- Emit one directive per inline comment; emit none when there are no actionable inline comments.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3).
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2}

### Inline Artifact Follow-Ups
- Format each artifact follow-up as an unescaped Markdown list item, `- :codex-followup[visible phrase]{prompt="Complete user request"}`; avoid closing brackets in the visible phrase and escape double quotes in the prompt.

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.
</app-context>

For requests to create or edit a standalone LaTeX document, use the built-in editor by default. Create or edit the .tex source with normal file tools, and open the saved file with open_in_codex unless it is already open or the user requests otherwise. Keep follow-up edits in that same file and editor. Use compile_latex_document after editing and fix source errors within its repair limits. Keep the editor open even when compilation fails; preserve the source and report unverified compilation or unsupported project requirements. Discover these tools if deferred. The native editor requires no LaTeX plugin or local TeX installation; do not install either for it. Ordinary math explanations stay in chat.

<INSTRUCTIONS>
# Global rules — Joshua

These apply on **every** project on this machine, in every session. Project-level
`AGENTS.md` files add to this; they do not replace it.

Keep this file short. It reloads on every message.

---

## Who

Joshua Fisseha — `contact@aspiringattorneys.com`. Builds **LSAT U** (lsatprep.study) and
the Aspiring Attorneys brand. Teaches the LSAT: ~25 one-to-one sessions a week plus
consultations. Windows 11; a MacBook Pro runs some sessions too, so paths differ between
them — never assume `/Users/joshuaf/...` resolves here.

## Where things live

- **AI OS / second brain:** `C:\Users\Joshu\dev\ai-os` — the Obsidian vault. `context/`,
  `wiki/`, `students/`, `corpus/`, `decisions/`, `brainstorms/`, `skills/`, `projects/`.
  Open this folder rather than starting with no folder, or memory cannot accumulate.
- **Skill catalog:** `dev/ai-os/skills/Codex` (179) and `skills/codex` (154), with
  `PARITY.md` declaring deliberate single-runtime skills and `INDEX.md` cataloging them.
- **LSAT U app:** repo `vnjkoxpl-42905/lsatu-684d89db` — React + Vite + TS + Tailwind +
  shadcn, Supabase backend, hosted on Lovable.
- **GitHub:** account `vnjkoxpl-42905` (auto-generated name, correct account).

## How to work with him

- **Do the whole task.** Deliver the finished thing, then say plainly what you skipped
  and why. Don't hand back a plan when the work was asked for.
- **Look before asking.** If the answer is on disk or reachable through a connected tool,
  go get it. He has Firecrawl, Google Workspace (`gws`), and `gh` — use them.
- **Say what's actually true.** Distinguish verified from assumed, every time. If a step
  failed or was skipped, lead with that. A confident wrong answer costs more than "I
  don't know yet."
- **Surface your own mistakes immediately**, including scope errors you notice mid-task.
- Absolute dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`), never "yesterday" or "last week".
- Don't re-ask what he already answered. Don't pad with options he didn't request.

- **Dictation fixes.** A message shaped like `word --> word` (any arrow, any spacing), or
  "save X in my vocabulary", is a Superwhisper correction. Invoke the `superwhisper` skill
  and apply it in that turn, whatever else is in progress.

## Writing as Joshua

Anything published under his name — course copy, lessons, emails, posts.

Plain, direct, confident. Short sentences. Teach the reasoning rather than asserting the
conclusion; this is a teaching brand and the reasoning *is* the product. Concrete beats
abstract. Never condescend to the reader.

**Never use:** "delve into", "dive deep", "unlock", "unleash", "harness the power of",
"in today's fast-paced world", "ever-evolving landscape", "it's not just X, it's Y",
"navigate the complexities", "at the end of the day", "elevate", "supercharge",
"game-changer", "seamless", "robust", "I hope this helps!", "Great question!",
"Certainly!". No em-dash pile-ups. No paragraph opening with "Moreover," /
"Furthermore," / "Additionally,". No emoji in professional writing unless asked.

Headers should say something, not label a category — "Why students miss this", not
"Analysis".

## Safety

- **Draft by default; send only when he says "send".** Email, messages, posts are drafted
  and shown to him. When he says "send it" (or equivalent) in chat, send it, then log it in
  `wiki/send-ledger.md`. Never send on your own initiative, and never treat a request to
  draft as a request to send.
- **Never delete** files, emails, or records without explicit confirmation.
- The Google Workspace grant is broad (it includes deleting all Drive files), so the
  restraint has to live in tool permissions, not in wording. A prompt is not a permission
  layer.
- Secrets stay in `.env` and the OS keyring. Never paste a key into a note, a commit, or
  a chat.

## Tools already connected

- **Firecrawl** — CLI + 28 skills. Prefer it over MCP; the hosted MCP server was removed
  on purpose (the key would sit in plaintext in `~/.Codex.json`).
- **Google Workspace** — `gws` CLI, GCP project `ai-os-joshua`. Gmail, Calendar, Drive,
  Docs, Sheets, Slides, Tasks, People.
- **GitHub** — `gh` CLI, authenticated.

## Cost discipline

`AGENTS.md` reloads on every message, so keep this file lean. Prefer CLIs to MCP servers
(an MCP server can cost ~18k tokens per message in tool definitions). `/clear` between
unrelated tasks. Run the `handoff` skill past ~25% context rather than waiting for
auto-compact.

# Jay 2 — operating instructions for Codex (ai-os)

The canonical root is the repository directory containing this file (`C:\Users\Joshu\dev\ai-os` on this Windows machine). Resolve paths from the repository root instead of assuming a saved Mac or Windows absolute path. This is the router: it holds pointers, not knowledge. Read it, then follow the routing map to the right file instead of searching blind. Twin for Claude Code: `CLAUDE.md`.

## Identity and mission

You are **Jay 2**, Joshua's executive assistant. This root is his EA workspace and command center. Joshua is the founder of Aspiring Attorneys and builder of LSAT U (lsatprep.study), a premium LSAT prep platform; he is the product, voice, and content authority. Your job: take operations, admin, drafting, and research off his plate so his time goes to teaching and building. Frame work as decisions and tradeoffs, not basics.

Standing duties, run from here without re-briefing: student operations (transcripts, assignments, follow-ups via `students/`), prospect and consultation correspondence (drafted in his voice, **never auto-sent unless a pre-approved template**), platform actions on lsatprep.study, session-note ingestion from Gmail/Drive, and keeping the wiki ledgers (`tasks`/`hot`/`log`) current so the next session starts oriented.

## Routing map

Paths are relative to the repository root.

| Need | Path |
|---|---|
| **Who Joshua is** (identity, preferences, contact) | `context/about-me.md` |
| **The business** (offers, money, channels, gaps) | `context/work.md` |
| **Current priorities** (the 90-day slate) | `context/priorities.md` |
| **What we decided and why** (locked decisions) | `decisions/log.md` |
| Freshest session state (hot cache) | `wiki/hot.md` |
| LLM Wiki schema (source, page, ingest/query/lint rules) | `system/schema/llm-wiki.md` |
| Master index · work ledger · dated history | `wiki/index.md` · `wiki/tasks.md` · `wiki/log.md` |
| Product ground truth (pointers to live backends) | `wiki/dashboard.md` |
| LSAT teaching knowledge | `corpus/index.md` |
| A student — profile, transcripts, work, correspondence | `students/<name>/` — start at `students/README.md` |
| Voice for anything a student or prospect reads | `wiki/teaching-voice.md` |
| Was it sent? (every outbound draft/send) | `wiki/send-ledger.md` — append-only; Gmail is authority |
| Who the students are (name, email, sessions, links) | `students/roster.generated.md` — regenerate, never hand-edit |
| Learned facts and preferences (automemory) | native store `~/.claude/projects/C--Users-Joshu-dev-ai-os/memory/` + `MEMORY.md` index |
| Skill / agent catalog | `skills/INDEX.md`, `agents/` |
| Systems Jay 2 can reach (registry) | `connections.md` — 7 data domains, mechanism/auth/freshness; read by `/audit` |
| Operator brain (how to think about automation) | `references/3ms-framework.md` — the Three Ms; walked weekly by `/level-up` |
| Automation build backlog (what to build next, ranked) | `references/automation-backlog.md` — corpus-derived gaps + tiers; feeds `/level-up` |
| How-it-works reference notes (methods, not state) | `references/` — also `references/claude-plus-codex.md`, `references/obsidian-command-center.md`, `references/second-brain-levels.md` |
| Web research and Firecrawl agents | `references/firecrawl.md` (guidelines in `references/firecrawl/`) |
| Immutable source evidence · intake queue | `raw/sources/` · `raw/inbox/` — one inbox, one archive |
| Archived web clips, with provenance + hashes | `raw/sources/clips/<slug>/` — clip + `PROVENANCE.md` + `SHA256SUMS` |
| Raw personal-data exports (Google Takeout, Gemini session transcripts) | `raw/data-about-me/` — unprocessed PII, git-ignored; never read wholesale |
| Design/plan thinking, dated (grill-me + interview outputs) | `brainstorms/` — supersedes the retired `aios/` reform folder |
| Session handoffs · chat exports | `handoffs/` — operational records, deliberately OUTSIDE `raw/`; `session-handoff` writes here |
| External teardowns and research, dated | `research/` |
| Web-clipped articles (Obsidian Web Clipper) | `raw/inbox/` — unprocessed only; `ingest` copies and hash-verifies them into `raw/sources/clips/`; processed originals stay until removal is authorized |
| Application code | `../ai-os-projects/lsatu/` — own repo, own instructions, own remote |
| Other projects (life-path, …) | `../ai-os-projects/<name>/` — each with its own `CLAUDE.md` + `.claude/` |

Application repositories and dependencies stay outside this Obsidian vault, in sibling `../ai-os-projects/`. Do not create a junction from the vault back into that directory.

## Retrieval order

1. `wiki/hot.md` — current-session narrative and open threads.
2. `wiki/index.md` → the page (teaching knowledge: `corpus/index.md`; a student: their folder). Follow links; there is no semantic search and none is needed at this size.
3. The live system — the final freshness escalation.

**Live systems are authority for operational state; the brain mirrors them:** Cal.com + Google Calendar own sessions scheduled/used, LSAT U Supabase owns homework status/dossier/publish state, Stripe owns payment events, Gmail owns correspondence. On any disagreement, the backend wins. The brain is primary — nothing upstream holds them — for transcripts, teaching notes, judgments, prep briefs, curriculum, product specs, and decisions.

**Do not read the wiki unless the task needs it.** Retrieval costs context every turn. Skip it for: code edits in `../ai-os-projects/lsatu/`; shell/Git/file ops; questions the injected memories already answer; a skill run that names its own inputs; anything mechanical and self-contained. Route to it for: what is X · what did we decide and why · who a student is and where they stand · anything drafted in Joshua's voice for someone else · any decision touching roadmap, pedagogy, or UX.

**LLM Wiki schema:** For knowledge intake, knowledge questions, durable synthesis, and wiki maintenance, follow `system/schema/llm-wiki.md`. Use `ingest` as the single intake entry point; keep sources immutable, compile into existing pages, update the complete fenced catalog in `wiki/index.md`, and append changes to `wiki/log.md`. Preserve domain homes and live-system authority. Mechanical tasks retain the retrieval exceptions above.

**Wiki operations (LLM-wiki pattern):** the LLM writes/maintains `wiki/` and `corpus/`; Joshua sources, explores, asks. Raw sources are immutable — read, never modify. *Ingest:* read the source from `raw/`, discuss takeaways, write/update the pages it touches, update `wiki/index.md`, append to `wiki/log.md` (`## [YYYY-MM-DD] ingest | Title`); one source at a time, supervised, unless Joshua says batch. *Query:* index first, then pages; file valuable answers back as pages so explorations compound. *Lint:* `second-brain-lint` for contradictions, stale claims, orphans, missing pages.

## Voice

- **No em-dashes, ever.** Joshua never types them; a stray em-dash reads as AI and costs trust.
- **No AI-slop vocabulary** — never "delve," "tapestry," "testament," "demystify," "boasts," "in the realm of," and their kin.
- **Anything a student or prospect will read** routes through `wiki/teaching-voice.md` and is drafted, never sent, unless it is a pre-approved template.
- **When an outbound message is authorized**, preserve the draft's paragraph breaks, list lines, and intentional spacing. After sending, compare the recipient-facing rendering with the draft and confirm exactly one copy landed. Report any mismatch; never resend automatically.
- **Lead with your recommendation, not a menu.** Be decisive; don't over-hedge.
- **Any prompt Joshua will paste elsewhere** goes inside a fenced code block, never inline prose.

## Tools, keys, and secrets

- **The entire secret model is `.env` + `.gitignore`.** The root `.env` (git-ignored — verify with `git check-ignore .env`) is Joshua's single central store for **everything**: API keys, passwords, and bank/account info (decided 2026-07-17). OAuth client secrets live in `~/.config/gws/`, outside the repo. There is no vault, no Keychain, no encrypted store (`records.sparsebundle` is dead) and none is wanted. Never paste a credential into chat — add it to `.env` directly in the editor.
- **Safety is the tool layer, not prompts:** allow/deny tool lists + scoped API keys. Jay 2 acts under its own credentials and never impersonates Joshua.
- **Connected live systems:** Cal.com, Google Calendar, LSAT U Supabase, Stripe, Gmail. Full registry in `connections.md`.
- **Google access is `gws` CLI only** (`gws gmail|drive|calendar|docs …`, keyring-auth; see `skills/codex/gws-shared/`). Never the Google connector MCPs — the CLI is faster, batchable, and exports Docs to markdown.
- **Government IDs stay outside this OS.** Everything else (student names, emails, schedules, transcripts, notes, payment *links*) is ordinary local working material — classify by content, never by filename.
- **Git remote is enabled.** `origin` is GitHub (`vnjkoxpl-42905/ai-os`, decided 2026-09-29). The outer repo never tracks `.env`, `../ai-os-projects/lsatu/` (own repo), runtime logs, or locks. Do not create gitlinks.
- **New laptop restore:** GitHub contains tracked ai-os files and skills. It deliberately excludes `.env`, `raw/`, app repos, credentials, and machine sessions. Restore machine-specific files from the private backup using `setup/backup/README.md` and its `README - START HERE.md`; install tools separately and sign in again where sessions cannot be restored. Never move credentials, raw personal data, or active browser tokens into GitHub.

## Skills

Everything is a skill — **there are no slash commands** (decided 2026-07-17: one kind, one home, one activation path). The catalog at `skills/` and `agents/` is inert storage; nothing auto-loads. An item runs only once **activated by copy** (not symlink) into `.agents/skills/` (Claude: `.claude/skills/`). Creating one writes to **both** the project and the catalog (`skills/{claude,codex}/`), project-scoped — never auto-global. `claude/` and `codex/` subtrees are never merged; a vendor item is a live symlink + a frozen `_snapshots/` copy. `system/scripts/check-skills.sh` validates the model; `skills/INDEX.md` indexes it.

Active in this root. Run `pickup` only when Joshua explicitly asks for it. Do not run it automatically at session start. Use `wrapup` at the end of substantive sessions:

| Skill | Use it when |
|---|---|
| `pickup` / `wrapup` | `pickup` only on Joshua's explicit request / `wrapup` at session end (wrapup persists to the wiki ledgers) |
| `session-handoff` | mid-work context reset near ~250k, or passing work Codex↔Claude — chat-only, writes nothing |
| `audit` | scoring the OS against the Four Cs (structural health, /100) |
| `level-up` | weekly 3Ms interview to find + ship one automation |
| `consultation-inquiry-drafts`, `-followup-drafts`, `inbound-tutoring-replies` | drafting to prospects/students — always via the teaching voice |
| `guided-drill-assignment` | assigning a student a drill |
| `lsat-u-platform-actions` | doing anything ON lsatprep.study from here (assign, post, message, ingest) |
| `tutorocean-profile-fill` | TutorOcean profile work |
| `prompt-architect-refiner` | refining a prompt before it ships |
| `accommodations-email` | "accommodations email to X" (dictation: "accommodations scale"); pre-approved send, QP form attached, self-logging |

When a skill run exposes a gap, improve the skill before moving on. Runtime-specific catalog differences must be justified in `skills/PARITY.md`; undeclared differences are defects.

## Guardrails

- **95% rule.** Make no changes until you are 95% confident what Joshua wants. Ask until you are.
- **Lovable credits require confirmation.** Never take an action that spends or may spend Lovable credits without Joshua's explicit confirmation immediately before the action. Do not infer approval from a broader request to fix, build, deploy, or continue. Free Lovable controls and direct deployment paths may be used without this credit-spend confirmation.
- **Lovable Cloud deploys through Lovable.** LSAT U currently uses a Lovable Cloud-managed backend. Deploy its Edge Functions through the Lovable agent, not the Supabase CLI, unless the backend has first been migrated to a separately managed Supabase project. Confirm this route with Joshua before starting a Lovable deployment.
- **Root stays thin.** Don't accumulate files at the root; work products go to their homes (wiki, students, corpus, projects). Anything left at root gets filed before the session ends.
- **Delegate bulk work.** Exploration or analysis spanning 3+ files goes to a sub-agent that returns summaries, not file dumps.
- **Shell ergonomics.** Run one command per call — chained `cmd; cmd` and `rm -rf X && clone Y` forms trip permission denials that the split commands would not. Never poll with `sleep`. Use backgrounded execution for anything slow, and raise the timeout explicitly for known-slow ops (large moves, typecheck-gated pushes, full verify runs) rather than eating the default.
- **Search before creating.** One authoritative page per subject — update it, don't grow a parallel truth. `wiki/index.md` catalogs every page and updates on every ingest.
- **Preserve provenance and source hashes.** Never move, delete, or modify a migration source root — copy and hash-verify. Never follow a source symlink outside its registered root.
- **Conflicts stay explicit until adjudicated** — never silently overwrite one source generation with another.
- **Automation writes only generated files or fenced generated sections,** through compare-and-swap.
- **Obey nested instruction files** — they win over broader ones for their subtree. LSATU's recovered `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` are inviolate: never regenerate them without Joshua's explicit approval.
- **Memory = native automemory.** "Remember that…" writes one fact per file to the native store; `MEMORY.md` indexes it. This file is the rules; memory is learned facts — never mix them. Transcripts and raw captures never auto-promote.
- **Append meaningful system changes** to `wiki/log.md`; log locked decisions to `decisions/log.md`.

## Dual-runtime (Codex + Claude)

- Begin at the Git-root `AGENTS.md` and follow directory-scoped instruction files toward the working path; the nearest file wins for its subtree.
- Keep root instructions inside the runtime byte budget. Move narrow rules to the narrowest owning directory rather than growing this file.
- Activated skills are **copies** in `.agents/skills/` (from `skills/codex/`); agent definitions convert to `.codex/agents/*.toml` with the instructions in `developer_instructions`.
- Claude reads `CLAUDE.md` and never this file. Anything that must hold for both runtimes goes in BOTH files — when you change it here, mirror it there; keep the routing map and guardrails byte-identical between them.
- Activation is unequal by design: Codex reads copies in `.agents/skills/`, Claude reads copies in `.claude/skills/`. Codex and Claude both activate the LLM Wiki ingest, query, and lint workflows. Other runtime-specific activation differences remain declared in `skills/PARITY.md`. Never have separate runtimes writing the same page concurrently.
- Never have Claude and Codex editing the same file at once; pass work between them by session handoff (summarize → clear → paste). At ~250k tokens, hand off rather than riding autocompact.

Omitted for legacy Activities authored\\r\\n   * before per-Activity rubrics existed; the edge function then applies its\\r\\n   * Negation Station default, which is what those Activities expect.\\r\\n   */\\r\\n  coach?: ActivityCoach;\\r\\n  /**\\r\\n   * A numbered checklist to judge coverage against, for drills where WHICH\\r\\n   * ideas survived is the feedback (The Press). Omit and no coverage comes\\r\\n   * back, which every other drill wants.\\r\\n   */\\r\\n  ideas?: { n: number; text: string }[];\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport interface JudgeResult {\\r\\n  ok: boolean;\\r\\n  verdict?: CoachVerdict;\\r\\n  error?: string;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/**\\r\\n * How long a student waits before the Coach is treated as unreachable. Long\\r\\n * enough for a slow model call, short enough that nobody sits looking at a\\r\\n * spinner wondering whether the page is broken.\\r\\n */\\r\\nconst COACH_TIMEOUT_MS = 12_000;\\r\\n\\r\\nexport function useActivityCoach() {\\r\\n  const [judging, setJudging] = useState(false);\\r\\n\\r\\n  const judge = useCallback(async ({ item, studentResponse, attemptNo, coach, ideas }: JudgeArgs): Promise<JudgeResult> => {\\r\\n    setJudging(true);\\r\\n    // A hung gateway used to leave the textarea disabled and the spinner\\r\\n    // spinning with no way out: no timeout, no abort, nothing for the student\\r\\n    // to do but reload and lose the answer. The item now falls through to the\\r\\n    // Coach-unavailable path, which reveals the credited answer and records the\\r\\n    // attempt unjudged.\\r\\n    const abort = new AbortController();\\r\\n    const timeout = setTimeout(() => abort.abort(), COACH_TIMEOUT_MS);\\r\\n    try {\\r\\n      const { data, error } = await supabase.functions.invoke(\\"activity-coach\\", {\\r\\n        signal: abort.signal,\\r\\n        body: {\\r\\n          statement: item.prompt,\\r\\n          studentResponse,\\r\\n          creditedAnswers: item.credited_answers,\\r\\n          explanation: item.explanation,\\r\\n          attemptNo,\\r\\n          coach,\\r\\n          category: item.category,\\r\\n          ideas,\\r\\n        },\\r\\n      });\\r\\n\\r\\n      if (error) {\\r\\n        const msg = error.message || \\"Coach unavailable\\";\\r\\n        console.error(\\"[activity-coach] invoke failed\\", error);\\r\\n        return { ok: false, error: msg };\\r\\n      }\\r\\n      if (!data || typeof data.verdict !== \\"string\\") {\\r\\n        console.error(\\"[activity-coach] malformed response\\", data);\\r\\n        return { ok: false, error: (data && data.error) || \\"Coach returned no verdict\\" };\\r\\n      }\\r\\n\\r\\n      // Coverage is only ever passed through, and only as an array of numbers.\\r\\n      // Anything else stays undefined so the checklist renders unjudged rather\\r\\n      // than claiming ticks nobody assigned.\\r\\n      const covered = Array.isArray(data.covered)\\r\\n        ? data.covered.filter((n: unknown) => typeof n === \\"number\\")\\r\\n        : undefined;\\r\\n\\r\\n      return { ok: true, verdict: { verdict: data.verdict, feedback: data.feedback ?? \\"\\", covered } };\\r\\n    } catch (e) {\\r\\n      if (abort.signal.aborted) {\\r\\n        console.error(\\"[activity-coach] timed out\\", { ms: COACH_TIMEOUT_MS });\\r\\n        return { ok: false, error: \\"Coach timed out\\" };\\r\\n      }\\r\\n      console.error(\\"[activity-coach] threw\\", e);\\r\\n      return { ok: false, error: e instanceof Error ? e.message : \\"Coach error\\" };\\r\\n    } finally {\\r\\n      clearTimeout(timeout);\\r\\n      setJudging(false);\\r\\n    }\\r\\n  }, []);\\r\\n\\r\\n  return { judge, judging };\\r\\n}\\r\\n"}'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{"chunk_id":"f9b045","wall_time_seconds":1.6771219,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":385,"output":"src/features/activity-centre/worlds/registry.tsx:119:   * author already wrote down. Nothing in this slice changes live records or enables those controls.\n+\n+The artifact at `artifacts/2026-09-30-activity-revocation.sql` adds independent `revoked_at` and `revoked_by`. Student response INSERT requires an available source owned by the same account. A response trigger locks the source with `FOR SHARE`, serializing recovery/insert against revocation's `FOR UPDATE`; even a service-role recovery insert cannot append evidence to a revoked source. Visible mirror inserts or unhides require an available source belonging to that mirror's student. Existing history remains stored for admin review. Hiding a mirror alone is still insufficient.\n+\n+## Wire the UI only after deployment verification\n+\n+`src/features/activity-centre/api/activityRevocation.ts` probes `activity_revocation_capability()`. Missing RPC, denied access, bad version, or network failure all return unavailable. The helper checks the current authenticated actor, passes the exact source/student IDs, and requires a matching receipt. It is deliberately not wired to a UI control in this slice.\n+\n+After deployment, add `revoked_at`/`revoked_by` to the assignment domain types and summary reader in `activitiesClient.ts`; generated Supabase types must be regenerated rather than hand-edited. Admin My Work/Dossier readers still see revoked source rows, so filter them from actionable projections or show a separate read-only historical row. `ActivityRunner.tsx` needs an early revocation gate for an admin viewing their own revoked assignment, because admin SELECT intentionally still sees the source; students already get no source row through RLS. Keep teacher historical inspection read-only. A mounted student's stale runner will fail source completion and response writes server-side after revocation.\n+\n+Enable controls in `HubAssignments.tsx` and `pages/teacher/students/DossierWork.tsx` only when the capability probe confirms version 1. Require the existing confirmation dialog, call the helper with the issued source ID and selected student ID, and refresh both the mirror query and scoped source feed after a confirmed receipt. Do not delete the Classroom mirror or the source row. An error must keep the record visible and must not say Unassigned. The local harness below uses only synthetic fixtures and is not proof that the live backend has been upgraded. Check existing policy names against the live catalog before installation: PostgreSQL permissive policies combine with OR, so an additional broad student policy would bypass the replacements. It exercises denied student calls and forged attribution, owner mutation denial, atomic rollback when mirror hiding fails, retained source/response/grade history, idempotence across two admins, blocked mirror resurrection, direct student reads/writes, service-level recovery denial, and new issuance after revocation. No runtime dependency was added to the app.\n+\n+The client Vitest suite checks capability failure, no mutation against an unsupported backend, expected subject/actor receipt validation, and idempotent attribution. These are contract checks; the executable SQL harness is the database behavior check.\n+\n+Known boundary: a student with broad Activity library access can choose a new library run. Revoking one issued source is not withdrawal of their entire Activity library entitlement. Audio storage and historical grade reads are not deleted or revoked by this source access operation. [{'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Script completed\nWall time 6.7 seconds\nOutput:\n'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{"chunk_id":"620221","wall_time_seconds":4.2607792,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":4134,"output":"# Ship the atomic PrepTest writer before standalone timed work\\r\\n\\r\\nDate: 2026-09-30\\r\\n\\r\\nStatus: **Implementation design only. No SQL, RPC, frontend switch, or backend deployment is implemented by this document.** Ticket #167 remains open. This expands [the proposed timed-write contract](2026-09-30-timed-write-contract.md); that contract\'s live metadata evidence and deployment approval requirements still apply.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe first backend release should cover PrepTest parent state, LR legs, RC legs, and the break together. Standalone timed LR/RC follows as a separate adoption phase. A parent-only RPC would leave the child-write race intact.\\r\\n\\r\\n## The existing boundaries determine the first batch\\r\\n\\r\\n| Existing boundary | Current behavior | Required v1 replacement |\\r\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\r\\n| `src/lib/practiceTestStore.ts` | Parent creation, revision CAS, device claim, pending device copies | Versioned create/claim commands and authoritative command responses; existing reads and backup ownership checks remain |\\r\\n| `src/lib/drillResumeSession.ts` | Separate parent-device check, then official LR KV snapshot upsert | LR snapshot checkpoint under the parent lock; retained device copy until acknowledgement |\\r\\n| `src/pages/Drill.tsx`, `src/lib/sectionHistorySave.ts` | LR closeout writes attempts, WAJ, history, resume completion in separate requests | One official close-leg command; explicit projection completion contract |\\r\\n| `src/features/rc/api/rcProgress.ts` | Session creation, answer insert, clock/position update, and completion each check/write separately | Typed RC start/checkpoint/close-leg commands |\\r\\n| `src/features/rc/pages/RcPlayer.tsx` | Questions and clock gated on account reads/saves; closeout writes blank first-attempt rows | Consume acknowledged session/position/clock; closeout batch and parent advance commit together |\\r\\n| `src/pages/PracticeTestRun.tsx` | Reads child results and later saves parent advancement/break/final score | Read authoritative parent returned by close-leg; parent and break commands cannot accept arbitrary JSON patches |\\r\\n| `src/lib/practiceTestRunner.ts`, `src/lib/practiceTestReview.ts` | Read attributed historical LR/RC records | Preserve result/review reads; v1 completion is not inferred from a child row that has not committed parent advancement |\\r\\n\\r\\nRepository schema is concrete but is not a fresh live DDL verification. `practice_test_runs.id` is **text**, not UUID. Its statuses are `in-progress`, `complete`, `abandoned`; RC uses `in_progress`, `completed`, `abandoned`. LR official records are JSON in `bootcamp_kv`, under `practice_sessions`; do not assume a normalized LR sessions table exists. Keep the installed owner FKs and per-leg/first-attempt unique indexes described in the contract.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Phase 0: freeze behavior and reproduce the races\\r\\n\\r\\nPrepare an ordinary-authenticated two-client harness against an isolated database with the installed schema. Refresh the live metadata inventory before deployment. Exercise existing parent CAS, then demonstrate that separate child preflight/writes can race takeover. No service-role success is permission evidence.\\r\\n\\r\\nRecord these current semantics before implementation:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Parent `section_seconds` freezes the user\'s chosen timing. The break is 600 seconds. Historical null timing retains existing reader compatibility.\\r\\n- LR permits overtime and records `regulation_answered_qids`. Preserve that distinction; do not silently introduce automatic submission at budget expiry.\\r\\n- RC answer column is `selected`; null closeout rows count as unanswered, and session elapsed time is not the sum of per-question times.\\r\\n- Current scoring is client-derived. This work protects transactional ownership, clock state, and acknowledged results. It does **not** introduce a new secure-grade product requirement or claim server-verified answer correctness. Validate result structure and derive parent totals from acknowledged child results. Preserve existing scoring formulas and explicitly retain their trust boundary.\\r\\n- Current LR closeout requires its expected WAJ work before the leg is considered finished. Do not move it after advancement without a separately recorded change to that behavior.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Phase 1: add protected control state and receipts\\r\\n\\r\\nPrepare two forward migrations, not a historical-record rewrite:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. `supabase/migrations/<timestamp>_timed_work_v1_control.sql`: control fields, receipt table, typed RPC helpers, and owner result reads.\\r\\n2. `supabase/migrations/<timestamp>_timed_work_v1_enforcement.sql`: v1 direct-write restrictions and exhaustive OLD/NEW attribution protection.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe exact timestamps are assigned when implementation starts. Managed-role CREATE\\r\\n-- ROLE/ownership support must be confirmed before any deployment is approved.\\r\\nbegin;\\r\\ndo $$ begin\\r\\n  if not exists(select 1 from pg_roles where rolname = \'timed_pt_executor\') then\\r\\n    create role timed_pt_executor nologin nosuperuser nocreatedb nocreaterole noinherit nobypassrls;\\r\\n  end if;\\r\\n  if exists(select 1 from pg_roles where rolname = \'timed_pt_executor\' and\\r\\n    (rolcanlogin or rolsuper or rolcreatedb or rolcreaterole or rolbypassrls)) or\\r\\n    pg_has_role(\'authenticated\', \'timed_pt_executor\', \'MEMBER\') or\\r\\n    pg_has_role(\'anon\', \'timed_pt_executor\', \'MEMBER\') then\\r\\n    raise exception \'Unsafe timed executor role configuration\';\\r\\n  end if;\\r\\nend $$;\\r\\ngrant usage on schema public, auth to timed_pt_executor;\\r\\n\\r\\ncreate function public.timed_pt_leg_definitions_v1(p_legs jsonb) returns jsonb\\r\\nlanguage sql immutable strict set search_path = pg_catalog as $$\\r\\n  select jsonb_agg(jsonb_strip_nulls(jsonb_build_object(\\r\\n    \'kind\', leg->\'kind\', \'section\', leg->\'section\', \'questionCount\', leg->\'questionCount\',\\r\\n    \'passageIds\', leg->\'passageIds\')) order by ordinal)\\r\\n  from jsonb_array_elements(p_legs) with ordinality as e(leg,ordinal)\\r\\n$$;\\r\\n\\r\\nalter table public.practice_test_runs\\r\\n  add column timed_contract_version smallint,\\r\\n  add column timed_writer_epoch bigint,\\r\\n  add column timed_phase text,\\r\\n  add column timed_elapsed_ms bigint,\\r\\n  add column timed_running_anchor timestamptz,\\r\\n  add column timed_lease_expires_at timestamptz,\\r\\n  add column timed_clock_leg integer,\\r\\n  add column timed_frozen_legs jsonb,\\r\\n  add column timed_lease_ms integer;\\r\\n\\r\\n-- No guessed lease constant or historical backfill. and timed_phase in (\'ready\',\'leg-running\',\'leg-paused\',\'closeout-pending\',\'break-running\',\'break-paused\',\'complete\',\'abandoned\')\\r\\n    and timed_elapsed_ms >= 0 and timed_lease_ms > (\'break-running\',\'break-paused\') and timed_clock_leg is null\\r\\n          and current_leg = break_after_leg and not break_taken)\\r\\n      or (timed_phase in (\'ready\',\'complete\',\'abandoned\') and timed_clock_leg is null))\\r\\n    and ((timed_phase = \'complete\' and status = \'complete\' and current_leg = jsonb_array_length(timed_frozen_legs)\\r\\n          and completed_at is not null)\\r\\n      or (timed_phase = \'abandoned\' and status = \'abandoned\')\\r\\n      or (timed_phase not in (\'complete\',\'abandoned\') and status = \'in-progress\' and completed_at is null))\\r\\n  ) is true\\r\\n);\\r\\n\\r\\ncreate table public.timed_pt_receipts_v1 (\\r\\n  owner_id uuid not null references auth.users(id),\\r\\n  work_kind text not null check (work_kind = \'practice-test\'),\\r\\n  work_id text not null,\\r\\n  command_id uuid not null,\\r\\n  canonical_command jsonb not null check (jsonb_typeof(canonical_command) = \'object\'),\\r\\n owner_id) references public.practice_test_runs(id,user_id)\\r\\n);\\r\\n\\r\\ncreate table public.timed_pt_lr_bindings_v1 (\\r\\n  owner_id uuid not null references auth.users(id),\\r\\n  run_id text null,\\r\\n  frozen_qids text[] not null check (cardinality(frozen_qids) > 0),\\r\\n  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),\\r\\n  primary key(run_id,leg_index),\\r\\n  unique(owner_id,namespace,record_id),\\r\\n  foreign key(run_id,owner_id) references public.practice_test_runs(id,user_id),\\r\\n  check(source_key = \'drill::practice-test::\' || run_id || \'::leg-\' Future definer\\r\\n-- RPCs must be owned by this dedicated role; unrelated postgres definers do not\\r\\n-- gain permission just because they bypass table RLS.\\r\\ncreate function public.guard_timed_pt_foundation_v1() returns trigger\\r\\nlanguage plpgsql set search_path = public as $$\\r\\nbegin\\r\\n  if TG_TABLE_NAME = \'practice_test_runs\' then\\r\\n    if (TG_OP <> \'INSERT\' and OLD.timed_contract_version is not null) or\\r\\n       (TG_OP <> \'DELETE\' and NEW.timed_contract_version is not null) then\\r\\n      if current_user <> \'timed_pt_executor\' then\\r\\n        raise exception \'Protected PrepTest requires the timed writer\' using errcode=\'42501\';\\r\\n      end if;\\r\\n      if TG_OP = \'DELETE\' then raise exception \'Protected PrepTest history cannot be deleted\' using errcode=\'42501\'; end if;\\r\\n      if TG_OP = \'UPDATE\' and OLD.timed_contract_version is not null then\\r\\n        if OLD.status in (\'complete\',\'abandoned\') and NEW is distinct from OLD then\\r\\n          raise exception \'Terminal PrepTest cannot change\' using errcode=\'42501\';\\r\\n        end if;\\r\\n        if NEW.user_id is distinct from OLD.user_id or NEW.id is distinct from OLD.id or\\r\\n          NEW.pt is distinct from OLD.pt or NEW.pace is distinct from OLD.pace or\\r\\n          NEW.section_seconds is distinct from OLD.section_seconds or\\r\\n          NEW.timed_contract_version is distinct from OLD.timed_contract_version or\\r\\n          NEW.timed_frozen_legs is distinct from OLD.timed_frozen_legs or\\r\\n          NEW.timed_lease_ms is distinct from OLD.timed_lease_ms or\\r\\n          NEW.break_after_leg is distinct from OLD.break_after_leg or\\r\\n          NEW.created_at is distinct from OLD.created_at then\\r\\n          raise exception \'PrepTest attribution and frozen definition are immutable\' using errcode=\'42501\';\\r\\n        end if;\\r\\n        if NEW.timed_writer_epoch < OLD.timed_writer_epoch or NEW.timed_writer_epoch > OLD.timed_writer_epoch + 1 or\\r\\n          NEW.revision <> OLD.revision + 1 or\\r\\n          (NEW.timed_clock_leg is not distinct from OLD.timed_clock_leg and NEW.timed_phase not in (\'ready\',\'complete\')\\r\\n           and NEW.timed_elapsed_ms < OLD.timed_elapsed_ms) or\\r\\n          (NEW.timed_phase in (\'complete\',\'abandoned\') and NEW.timed_elapsed_ms < OLD.timed_elapsed_ms) then\\r\\n          raise exception \'PrepTest control cannot move backwards\' using errcode=\'42501\';\\r\\n        end if;\\r\\n      end if;\\r\\n    end if;\\r\\n  else\\r\\n    if current_user <> \'timed_pt_executor\' or TG_OP <> \'INSERT\' then\\r\\n      raise exception \'Timed bindings and receipts are append-only executor records\' using errcode=\'42501\';\\r\\n    end if;\\r\\n    if TG_TABLE_NAME = \'timed_pt_receipts_v1\' then\\r\\n      NEW.command_hash := encode(sha256(convert_to(NEW.canonical_command::text, \'UTF8\')), \'hex\');\\r\\n      if not exists(select 1 from public.practice_test_runs p where p.id=NEW.work_id and p.user_id=NEW.owner_id\\r\\n          and p.timed_contract_version=1 and p.revision=NEW.committed_revision) then\\r\\n        raise exception \'Receipt must name the committed protected revision\' using errcode=\'42501\';\\r\\n      end if;\\r\\n    end if;\\r\\n    if TG_TABLE_NAME = \'timed_pt_lr_bindings_v1\' then\\r\\n    if not exists(\\r\\n      select 1 from public.practice_test_runs p where p.id=NEW.run_id and p.user_id=NEW.owner_id\\r\\n        and p.timed_contract_version=1 and NEW.leg_index < jsonb_array_length(p.timed_frozen_legs)\\r\\n        and p.timed_frozen_legs->NEW.leg_index->>\'kind\'=\'lr\'\\r\\n        and (p.timed_frozen_legs->NEW.leg_index->>\'questionCount\')::integer=cardinality(NEW.frozen_qids)\\r\\n    ) then\\r\\n      raise exception \'LR binding must match a protected frozen leg\' using errcode=\'42501\';\\r\\n    end if;\\r\\n    if (exists(select 1 from unnest(NEW.frozen_qids) q where q is null or q=\'\') or\\r\\n       cardinality(NEW.frozen_qids) <> (select count(distinct q) from unnest(NEW.frozen_qids) q)) then\\r\\n      raise exception \'Frozen LR queue must contain distinct nonempty identities\' using errcode=\'42501\';\\r\\n    end if;\\r\\n    end if;\\r\\n  end if;\\r\\n  if TG_OP=\'DELETE\' then return OLD; end if;\\r\\n  return NEW;\\r\\nend $$;\\r\\ncreate trigger timed_pt_foundation_guard before insert or update or delete on public.practice_test_runs\\r\\n  for each row execute function public.guard_timed_pt_foundation_v1();\\r\\ncreate trigger timed_pt_receipt_guard before insert or update or delete on public.timed_pt_receipts_v1\\r\\n  for each row execute function public.guard_timed_pt_foundation_v1();\\r\\ncreate trigger timed_pt_binding_guard before insert or update or delete on public.timed_pt_lr_bindings_v1\\r\\n  for each row execute function public.guard_timed_pt_foundation_v1();\\r\\n\\r\\nalter table public.timed_pt_receipts_v1 enable row level security;\\r\\nalter table public.timed_pt_lr_bindings_v1 enable row level security;\\r\\nrevoke all on public.timed_pt_receipts_v1, public.timed_pt_lr_bindings_v1 from public,anon,authenticated;\\r\\ngrant select on public.timed_pt_receipts_v1, public.timed_pt_lr_bindings_v1 to authenticated;\\r\\ngrant select,insert,update on public.practice_test_runs to timed_pt_executor;\\r\\ngrant select,insert on public.timed_pt_receipts_v1, public.timed_pt_lr_bindings_v1 to timed_pt_executor;\\r\\ncreate policy timed_pt_executor on public.practice_test_runs for all to timed_pt_executor using(true) with check(true);\\r\\ncreate policy receipt_owner_read on public.timed_pt_receipts_v1 for select to authenticated using(owner_id=auth.uid());\\r\\ncreate policy binding_owner_read on public.timed_pt_lr_bindings_v1 for select to authenticated using(owner_id=auth.uid());\\r\\ncreate policy receipt_executor on public.timed_pt_receipts_v1 for insert to timed_pt_executor with check(true);\\r\\ncreate policy receipt_executor_read on public.timed_pt_receipts_v1 for select to timed_pt_executor using(true);\\r\\ncreate policy binding_executor on public.timed_pt_lr_bindings_v1 for insert to timed_pt_executor with check(true);\\r\\ncreate policy binding_executor_read on public.timed_pt_lr_bindings_v1 for select to timed_pt_executor using(true);\\r\\ncommit;\\r\\n"}'}]

[{'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Script completed\nWall time 12.0 seconds\nOutput:\n'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{"chunk_id":"adb61e","wall_time_seconds":5.9765311,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":4134,"output":"# Ship the atomic PrepTest writer before standalone timed work\\r\\n\\r\\nDate: 2026-09-30\\r\\n\\r\\nStatus: **Implementation design only. No SQL, RPC, frontend switch, or backend deployment is implemented by this document.** Ticket #167 remains open. This expands [the proposed timed-write contract](2026-09-30-timed-write-contract.md); that contract\'s live metadata evidence and deployment approval requirements still apply.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe first backend release should cover PrepTest parent state, LR legs, RC legs, and the break together. Standalone timed LR/RC follows as a separate adoption phase. A parent-only RPC would leave the child-write race intact.\\r\\n\\r\\n## The existing boundaries determine the first batch\\r\\n\\r\\n| Existing boundary | Current behavior | Required v1 replacement |\\r\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\r\\n| `src/lib/practiceTestStore.ts` | Parent creation, revision CAS, device claim, pending device copies | Versioned create/claim commands and authoritative command responses; existing reads and backup ownership checks remain |\\r\\n| `src/lib/drillResumeSession.ts` | Separate parent-device check, then official LR KV snapshot upsert | LR snapshot checkpoint under the parent lock; retained device copy until acknowledgement |\\r\\n| `src/pages/Drill.tsx`, `src/lib/sectionHistorySave.ts` | LR closeout writes attempts, WAJ, history, resume completion in separate requests | One official close-leg command; explicit projection completion contract |\\r\\n| `src/features/rc/api/rcProgress.ts` | Session creation, answer insert, clock/position update, and completion each check/write separately | Typed RC start/checkpoint/close-leg commands |\\r\\n| `src/features/rc/pages/RcPlayer.tsx` | Questions and clock gated on account reads/saves; closeout writes blank first-attempt rows | Consume acknowledged session/position/clock; closeout batch and parent advance commit together |\\r\\n| `src/pages/PracticeTestRun.tsx` | Reads child results and later saves parent advancement/break/final score | Read authoritative parent returned by close-leg; parent and break commands cannot accept arbitrary JSON patches |\\r\\n| `src/lib/practiceTestRunner.ts`, `src/lib/practiceTestReview.ts` | Read attributed historical LR/RC records | Preserve result/review reads; v1 completion is not inferred from a child row that has not committed parent advancement |\\r\\n\\r\\nRepository schema is concrete but is not a fresh live DDL verification. `practice_test_runs.id` is **text**, not UUID. Its statuses are `in-progress`, `complete`, `abandoned`; RC uses `in_progress`, `completed`, `abandoned`. LR official records are JSON in `bootcamp_kv`, under `practice_sessions`; do not assume a normalized LR sessions table exists. Keep the installed owner FKs and per-leg/first-attempt unique indexes described in the contract.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Phase 0: freeze behavior and reproduce the races\\r\\n\\r\\nPrepare an ordinary-authenticated two-client harness against an isolated database with the installed schema. Refresh the live metadata inventory before deployment. Exercise existing parent CAS, then demonstrate that separate child preflight/writes can race takeover. No service-role success is permission evidence.\\r\\n\\r\\nRecord these current semantics before implementation:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Parent `section_seconds` freezes the user\'s chosen timing. The break is 600 seconds. Historical null timing retains existing reader compatibility.\\r\\n- LR permits overtime and records `regulation_answered_qids`. Preserve that distinction; do not silently introduce automatic submission at budget expiry.\\r\\n- RC answer column is `selected`; null closeout rows count as unanswered, and session elapsed time is not the sum of per-question times.\\r\\n- Current scoring is client-derived. This work protects transactional ownership, clock state, and acknowledged results. It does **not** introduce a new secure-grade product requirement or claim server-verified answer correctness. Validate result structure and derive parent totals from acknowledged child results. Preserve existing scoring formulas and explicitly retain their trust boundary.\\r\\n- Current LR closeout requires its expected WAJ work before the leg is considered finished. Do not move it after advancement without a separately recorded change to that behavior.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Phase 1: add protected control state and receipts\\r\\n\\r\\nPrepare two forward migrations, not a historical-record rewrite:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. `supabase/migrations/<timestamp>_timed_work_v1_control.sql`: control fields, receipt table, typed RPC helpers, and owner result reads.\\r\\n2. `supabase/migrations/<timestamp>_timed_work_v1_enforcement.sql`: v1 direct-write restrictions and exhaustive OLD/NEW attribution protection.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe exact timestamps are assigned when implementation starts. Keep deployment of enforcement and adapter activation coordinated; an RPC left beside unrestricted protected raw writes does not provide the guarantee.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor the PT phase add nullable `timed_contract_version` to `practice_test_runs`, plus server-owned writer epoch, phase, accumulated elapsed milliseconds, running anchor, lease expiry, and active clock leg. Keep existing `revision` as the single command CAS version. Preserve existing device ID for UI display; possession of an arbitrary device ID alone does not authorize a write. Epoch/lease/revision are validated under the parent lock.\\r\\n\\r\\nConstraints for protected rows:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Version is supported; revision/epoch/elapsed are nonnegative.\\r\\n- Running phases have an anchor and lease; paused/terminal phases have no running anchor.\\r\\n- Clock leg matches the current frozen leg, or the phase is the one permitted break.\\r\\n- Owner, PT, pace, section duration, frozen leg definition, and protected version cannot be changed by a client patch.\\r\\n- Terminal state cannot reopen. No protected source or completion record is deleted by this API.\\r\\n\\r\\nUse a companion binding table for LR KV records. Its owner/run/leg, namespace, record ID, and frozen queue identity are immutable, and there is one binding per PT LR leg. The existing key `drill::practice-test::<runId>::leg-<index>` and `practiceSessionIdFor` can be preserved for PT compatibility. A generic owner JSON blob must not become writer/access authority.\\r\\n\\r\\nUse a durable command receipt table with unique `(owner_id, work_kind, work_id, command_id)`, canonical payload hash, committed revision, and committed result. A command UUID is separate from an RC attempt UUID. Store receipts in the same transaction as progress. Authenticated clients can read their own receipts but cannot insert/update/delete them directly. Retain receipts long enough for supported recovery; a TTL policy is not part of this batch.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Phase 2: implement one typed PT transaction\\r\\n\\r\\nPublic entry points: `create_timed_practice_test_v1` and `commit_timed_work_v1`. Creation cannot take an arbitrary owner. New protected children are created inside start-leg, not by direct browser inserts.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe commit envelope is `{workKind, workId, expectedRevision, writerEpoch, deviceId, commandId, operation, payload}`. Derive owner from `auth.uid()`. Parse only the fields for the named operation and reject unknown/immutable patches. Start with PT operations: claim/adopt, start-leg, checkpoint, pause, resume, close-leg, start-break, finish-break, abandon. Final completion is derived when the final leg closes; there is no unrestricted set-score or set-current-leg operation.\\r\\n\\r\\nEach successful command performs these steps:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Resolve the actor-owned parent and lock it `FOR UPDATE`. Look for the command receipt under that lock. A matching receipt acknowledges the old committed operation before stale-revision or current-access rejection; changed payload rejects. Return both the receipt and **current** authoritative parent so retrying an old receipt cannot restore an older UI state.\\r\\n2. Validate supported version, expected revision, writer epoch, lease, exact phase/leg, and immutable child binding. A new stale command returns a typed conflict with current state and makes no progress writes.\\r\\n3. Check current PT entitlement using the existing `can_sit_practice_test` rules. Lock the actual grant row used for authorization: [REDACTED] profile feature row, exact owned/unlocked/nonarchived assignment, or admin-role row. A boolean precheck alone does not serialize a concurrent revoke. Use deterministic lock order and test it against the revocation paths. Missing access rejects new writes while preserving history and receipts.\\r\\n4. Settle clock time using server time, bounded by the acknowledged lease expiry, then apply the operation. Never decrease elapsed time. Heartbeat renews only a valid active writer. Proposed 15-second heartbeat/45-second lease remains a proposal to verify, not an adopted product constant.\\r\\n5. Persist LR snapshot or RC answer batch together with elapsed time and position. Validate qid membership, queue order, question count, selected letters/nulls, index bounds, and exact parent/leg/session attribution. Do not regenerate missing content or accept a new queue during recovery. Keep all acknowledged choices through takeover.\\r\\n6. On close-leg, persist the official child result, required closeout projections, child terminal state, parent leg result, and advance/break/final state in one transaction. Increment parent revision once, write receipt, and return parent plus child checkpoint and server time.\\r\\n\\r\\nRC retains existing first-attempt uniqueness. Same attempt UUID with the same owner/session/question/passage/choice is idempotent; different content rejects. A different first-attempt UUID for an already committed question conflicts rather than replacing the original. Review reanswers require their separate allowed semantics and cannot reopen an exam leg. Clock checkpoint and answer acknowledgement must share the command; current split calls are not enough.\\r\\n\\r\\nLR stores the frozen `PracticeSession` shape and validates stable attribution outside that JSON. Do not trust supplied `user_id`, `pool_slug`, `completion_id`, or arbitrary section-history parent links. Keep unanswered/answered/overtime distinctions and current score trust. Validate totals against the frozen queue and derive parent aggregation from the acknowledged child record rather than a later unrelated readback.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor LR WAJ/analytics, inventory `commitSessionAttempts`, `logSectionWrongAnswers`, and `persistSectionResults` before moving their writes. Either put mandatory rows in the transaction, or introduce an explicit closeout-pending phase with an idempotent transactionally enqueued projection job. In the latter design, parent advancement still waits for required projection acknowledgement. Mail remains optional and cannot block the official leg, matching current behavior. Do not leave the existing client closeout path writing official rows around the RPC.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Phase 3: close direct-write bypasses before switching clients\\r\\n\\r\\nProtected parent INSERT/UPDATE, attributed LR KV INSERT/UPDATE, RC session/attempt INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, and official section-result INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE must reject ordinary authenticated direct mutations. Restrict metadata-only RC operations deliberately rather than accidentally disabling exclusions/review flags. Preserve ordinary bootcamp data and historical reads.\\r\\n\\r\\nEnforcement checks **OLD and NEW** protection, owner, source identity, and attribution. Clearing the PT FK, setting contract version null, moving a protected KV record, or inserting an alternate child for the same protected leg cannot escape it. Reserved PT LR source keys cannot be recreated through generic KV writes. Replace conflicting permissive policies; adding a stricter permissive policy leaves the existing owner policy effective.\\r\\n\\r\\nPrefer a dedicated tightly privileged no-login executor role for protected RPCs if Lovable\'s managed migration role supports that ownership setup. Authenticated/anonymous must have no membership in it. Security-definer functions fix search path, qualify tables, check `auth.uid()`, and receive only narrow grants. Ordinary callers must not be able to forge an RPC-only bypass with a custom setting. Verify managed-role capabilities before selecting an enforcement technique; do not equate every `postgres`-owned definer function with this authorized writer.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Phase 4: switch PT adapters and explicitly adopt active work\\r\\n\\r\\nAdd `src/lib/timedWorkClient.ts` for typed command envelopes/responses and conflict/access/expired-writer errors. Backups retain the same pending command UUID, payload, expected revision, and epoch until acknowledged. Never mint a fresh command on a lost-response retry.\\r\\n\\r\\nSwitch the existing boundaries in the first table. The parent returned by close-leg drives advancement; `PracticeTestRun.tsx` stops performing a second parent save for that v1 leg. `RcPlayer.tsx` and `Drill.tsx` stop clocks and hide/gate questions on loss of authoritative writer state until claim/recovery is acknowledged. Otherwise a full section is identified by the section itself; a\\r\\n * filtered drill by the filters that drew it; Smart Drill by nothing but its\\r\\n * mode, because it has a single continuous run per student. Returns null for\\r\\n * the surfaces that own their own resume rows (guided, practice sets) and for\\r\\n * anything launched from an explicit list of qids, where the caller already\\r\\n"}'}]

It is not a long drill: the\\r\\n * composition is fixed, the order is the published one, and nothing is revealed\\r\\n * until the whole sitting is over.\\r\\n *\\r\\n * The run is saved to the student\'s account by practiceTestStore. The same 35:00 both section kinds run. */\\r\\nexport const PRACTICE_TEST_SECTION_SECONDS = 35 * 60;\\r\\n\\r\\n/** The break the real test gives you, after the second scored section. */\\r\\nexport const PRACTICE_TEST_BREAK_SECONDS = 10 * 60;\\r\\n\\r\\n/**\\r\\n * An LR section below this is a partial capture, not a section. The odd one out was this list.\\r\\n */\\r\\nconst PACE_LABELS: Record<PracticeTestPaceId, string> = {\\r\\n  standard: \'Standard\',\\r\\n  \'time-and-a-half\': \'Time and a half\',\\r\\n  \'double-time\': \'Double time\',\\r\\n  untimed: \'Untimed\',\\r\\n};\\r\\n\\r\\n/**\\r\\n * Each pace as a percentage of the student\'s OWN standard clock, not of 35:00.\\r\\n *\\r\\n * These were absolute before: \'standard\' was hard-wired to 35 minutes whatever\\r\\n * the student\'s standing timing mode said. A student carrying extra time who\\r\\n * picked \\"Standard\\" was handed a 35-minute section, which is less time than\\r\\n * they are entitled to, across a whole two-hour sitting. The section door has\\r\\n * always read the setting (SectionSelector\'s baseMinutes); the practice test\\r\\n * door never did, so the same two words meant two different clocks in one room.\\r\\n *\\r\\n * 100% is whatever their standing default is, so \\"Standard\\" means \\"my normal\\r\\n * section\\" for everyone.\\r\\n */\\r\\nconst PACE_PERCENT: Record<PracticeTestPaceId, number | null> = {\\r\\n  standard: 100,\\r\\n  \'time-and-a-half\': 150,\\r\\n  \'double-time\': 200,\\r\\n  untimed: null,\\r\\n};\\r\\n\\r\\n/** The pace\'s display name. The clock it implies depends on the student. */\\r\\nexport function practiceTestPaceLabel(id: PracticeTestPaceId): string {\\r\\n  return PACE_LABELS[id] ?? PACE_LABELS.standard;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/** Seconds one section runs for at this pace, off the student\'s own base. */\\r\\nexport function practiceTestSectionSeconds(\\r\\n  pace: PracticeTestPaceId,\\r\\n  baseSeconds: number = PRACTICE_TEST_SECTION_SECONDS,\\r\\n): number | null {\\r\\n  // Not `??`: untimed\'s percent IS null, and a nullish fallback would quietly\\r\\n  // turn \\"no clock\\" into the standard one. Only an unrecognised id falls back.\\r\\n  const percent = pace in PACE_PERCENT ? PACE_PERCENT[pace] : PACE_PERCENT.standard;\\r\\n  if (percent === null) return null;\\r\\n  return Math.round((baseSeconds * percent) / 100);\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/** The pace options for a student whose own standard section is `baseSeconds`. */\\r\\nexport function practiceTestPaces(baseSeconds: number = PRACTICE_TEST_SECTION_SECONDS): {\\r\\n  id: PracticeTestPaceId;\\r\\n  label: string;\\r\\n  /** Seconds per section. Null when untimed. */\\r\\n  sectionSeconds: number | null;\\r\\n}[] {\\r\\n  return (Object.keys(PACE_LABELS) as PracticeTestPaceId[]).map((id) => ({\\r\\n    id,\\r\\n    label: PACE_LABELS[id],\\r\\n    sectionSeconds: practiceTestSectionSeconds(id, baseSeconds),\\r\\n  }));\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/**\\r\\n * What a run\'s sections actually run for. Runs\\r\\n * created before this was stored fall back to the old absolute reading.\\r\\n */\\r\\nexport function practiceTestRunSectionSeconds(run: PracticeTestRun): number | null {\\r\\n  return run.sectionSeconds !== undefined\\r\\n    ? run.sectionSeconds\\r\\n    : practiceTestSectionSeconds(run.pace);\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport type PracticeTestLegKind = \'lr\' | \'rc\';\\r\\n\\r\\nexport interface PracticeTestLeg {\\r\\n  kind: PracticeTestLegKind;\\r\\n  /** The section number it carried on the real PrepTest. */\\r\\n  section: number;\\r\\n  /** Questions in this leg — what it contributes to the raw score. */\\r\\n  questionCount: number;\\r\\n  /** RC only: the four passages, in published order. */\\r\\n  passageIds?: number[];\\r\\n  /** ISO stamp set when the student begins this leg. */\\r\\n  startedAt?: string;\\r\\n  /** ISO stamp set when its result is read back. */\\r\\n  completedAt?: string;\\r\\n  correct?: number;\\r\\n  answered?: number;\\r\\n  timeMs?: number;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport type PracticeTestStatus = \'in-progress\' | \'complete\' | \'abandoned\';\\r\\n\\r\\nexport interface PracticeTestRun {\\r\\n  id: string;\\r\\n  /** Account owner. const pct = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, raw / total));\\r\\n  for (let i = 1; i < SCALE_ANCHORS.length; i += 1) {\\r\\n    const [prevRaw, prevScaled] = SCALE_ANCHORS[i - 1];\\r\\n    const [nextRaw, nextScaled] = SCALE_ANCHORS[i];\\r\\n    const prevPct = prevRaw / ANCHOR_TOTAL;\\r\\n    const nextPct = nextRaw / ANCHOR_TOTAL;\\r\\n    if (pct <= nextPct) {\\r\\n      if (nextPct === prevPct) return nextScaled;\\r\\n      const t = (pct - prevPct) / (nextPct - prevPct);\\r\\n      return Math.round(prevScaled + t * (nextScaled - prevScaled));\\r\\n    }\\r\\n  }\\r\\n  return Managed CREATE ROLE,\n -- ALTER OWNER and narrow grant support must be confirmed before deployment.\n+-- PostgreSQL 16+ creators can receive ADMIN membership without SET permission.\n+-- Preserve any preexisting direct membership options; restore them afterwards.\n+create temporary table timed_pt_bootstrap_membership_v1 on commit drop as\n+  select current_user::text as migration_role,m.admin_option,m.inherit_option,m.set_option\n+  from (select 1) seed left join pg_auth_members m on m.roleid=(select oid from pg_roles where rolname='timed_pt_executor')\n+    and m.member=(select oid from pg_roles where rolname=current_user);\n+do $$ declare state record; begin\n+  select * into state from timed_pt_bootstrap_membership_v1;\n+  if not pg_has_role(current_user,'timed_pt_executor','SET') then\n+    execute format('grant timed_pt_executor to %I with set true',state.migration_role);\n+  end if;\n+end $$;\n grant create on schema public to timed_pt_executor;\n@@\n revoke create on schema public from timed_pt_executor;\n+do $$ declare state record; begin\n+  select * into state from timed_pt_bootstrap_membership_v1;\n+  if state.admin_option is null then\n+    execute format('revoke timed_pt_executor from %I',state.migration_role);\n+  else\n+    execute format('grant timed_pt_executor to %I with set %s',state.migration_role,state.set_option);\n+    execute format('grant timed_pt_executor to %I with inherit %s',state.migration_role,state.inherit_option);\n+  end if;\n+end $$;\n*** End Patch"));

[{'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Script completed\nWall time 1.8 seconds\nOutput:\n'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{"chunk_id":"704624","wall_time_seconds":1.5947843000000002,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":918,"output":"    id?: string;\\r\\n    qid: string;\\r\\n    correct: boolean;\\r\\n    time_ms: number;\\r\\n    qtype: string;\\r\\n    level: number;\\r\\n    confidence: number | null;\\r\\n    mode: DrillMode;\\r\\n    selected_answer?: string;\\r\\n  }): Promise<boolean> => {\\r\\n    const question = questionBank.getQuestion(attemptData.qid);\\r\\n    if (!question) {\\r\\n      throw new Error(`saveAttemptToDatabase: unknown qid ${attemptData.qid}`);\\r\\n    }\\r\\n\\r\\n    if (!classId && classIdLoading) {\\r\\n      console.warn(\'saveAttemptToDatabase called before classId resolved, skipping\');\\r\\n      return false;\\r\\n    }\\r\\n    const resolvedClassId = classId || user?.id || \'\';\\r\\n    if (!resolvedClassId) {\\r\\n      throw new Error(\\r\\n        `saveAttemptToDatabase: no class_id and no user.id for qid ${attemptData.qid}`,\\r\\n      );\\r\\n    }\\r\\n    try {\\r\\n      const { error } = await supabase.from(\'attempts\').insert({\\r\\n        ...(attemptData.id ? { id: attemptData.id } : {}),\\r\\n        user_id: user?.id,\\r\\n        class_id: resolvedClassId,\\r\\n        qid: attemptData.qid,\\r\\n        pt: question.pt,\\r\\n        section: question.section,\\r\\n        qnum: question.qnum,\\r\\n        qtype: attemptData.qtype,\\r\\n        level: attemptData.level,\\r\\n        correct: attemptData.correct,\\r\\n        time_ms: attemptData.time_ms,\\r\\n        confidence: attemptData.confidence,\\r\\n        mode: attemptData.mode,\\r\\n        selected_answer: attemptData.selected_answer || null,\\r\\n        timestamp_iso: new Date().toISOString(),\\r\\n      });\\r\\n\\r\\n      if (error) {\\r\\n        // Guided sittings use a stable id for each question. A retry after the\\r\\n        // server accepted an earlier insert is the same attempt, not new work.\\r\\n        if (attemptData.id && error.code === \'23505\') return true;\\r\\n        console.error(\'[drill:saveAttempt] supabase insert failed\', {\\r\\n          userId: user?.id,\\r\\n          qid: attemptData.qid,\\r\\n          mode: attemptData.mode,\\r\\n          error,\\r\\n        });\\r\\n        throw new Error(`saveAttemptToDatabase: insert failed (${error.message})`);\\r\\n      }\\r\\n      return true;\\r\\n    } catch (err) {\\r\\n      console.error(\'[drill:saveAttempt] threw\', {\\r\\n        userId: user?.id,\\r\\n        qid: attemptData.qid,\\r\\n        mode: attemptData.mode,\\r\\n        err,\\r\\n      });\\r\\n      throw err;\\r\\n    }\\r\\n  };\\r\\n\\r\\n  // UI-level helper for the per-question submit handlers. Wraps the throwing\\r\\n  // service so the callers\' `if (!saved.ok)` toast logic keeps working — the\\r\\n  // error is logged at the service AND visible to the user via the caller\'s\\r\\n  // toast. This does NOT silently swallow: failures are logged, classified\\r\\n  // where the error still exists, and surfaced through the typed result.\\r\\n  type PersistResult =\\r\\n    | { ok: true }\\r\\n    | { ok: false; errorKind: \'auth\' | \'network\' | \'db\' | \'unknown\' };\\r\\n  const classifyPersistError = (e: unknown): \'auth\' | \'network\' | \'db\' | \'unknown\' => {\\r\\n    const message = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e ?? \'\');\\r\\n    if (/no class_id and no user\\\\.id|jwt|auth|401|403/i.test(message)) return \'auth\';\\r\\n    if (/fetch|network|timeout|Failed to fetch/i.test(message)) return \'network\';\\r\\n    if (/insert failed|supabase|postgres|duplicate|violates/i.test(message)) return \'db\';\\r\\n    return \'unknown\';\\r\\n  };\\r\\n  // Structured failure event. No PII: no user id, no answer text. There is no\\r\\n  // error-reporting sink in this repo as of 2026-09-12, so `console.error` is\\r\\n  // the sink; swap it here when one lands.\\r\\n  const reportCommitFailure = (event: {\\r\\n    qid: string;\\r\\n    launchKind: string | undefined;\\r\\n    transition: string;\\r\\n    errorKind: \'auth\' | \'network\' | \'db\' | \'unknown\';\\r\\n    deduped: boolean;\\r\\n  }) => {\\r\\n    console.error(\'[drill:commit-failed]\', event);\\r\\n  };\\r\\n"}'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{}'}]
